title: Answer engines
hired_for: To make AI assistants name us, describe us correctly and cite our pages when buyers ask what to buy.

jobs.job: Make AI assistants describe us correctly
jobs.why: When a buyer asks ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity or Google's AI about us, a wrong price, a wrong return policy or a wrong product loses the sale before they reach the site.

watch.metric: share of assistant answers that name the brand with correct facts, on the fixed prompt set, monthly, by assistant
watch.source: brand brain: monthly prompt-run log (a fixed set of buyer questions asked of each assistant; no platform reports this, so it is the closest proxy)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of 4 assistants name us, but 2 give an old return window. After: facts fixed at the source, 90% of answers are correct at the next monthly run.

jobs.job: Publish one facts page that answers what buyers ask assistants
jobs.why: Assistants fill gaps with guesses or old pages. One clear page with price, materials, sizing, shipping, returns and warranty gives them the right answer to repeat.

watch.metric: fact gaps from the last prompt audit that now have a published answer
watch.source: brand brain: monthly prompt-run log (a fixed set of buyer questions asked of each assistant; no platform reports this, so it is the closest proxy)

drives.metric: share of assistant answers that name the brand with correct facts

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 11 facts buyers ask about have no clear page. After: a facts page answers all 11 and gaps closed reads 100%.

jobs.job: Let AI search bots read our pages
jobs.why: If the site blocks the bots that AI assistants use to fetch pages, or hides text behind scripts, the brand cannot be cited no matter how good the pages are.

watch.metric: key pages reachable by AI search bots, weekly check
watch.source: robots file and firewall settings (Cloudflare) checked with a bot fetch test, plus server logs

drives.metric: share of assistant answers that cite our site

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the firewall blocks 2 AI search bots on all pages. After: search bots allowed, checkout still blocked, 100% of key pages reachable.

jobs.job: Keep our facts the same everywhere an assistant can read them
jobs.why: Assistants mix sources. If the site says 60-day returns and a marketplace listing says 30, they may repeat the wrong one.

watch.metric: facts that match on site, product feed, marketplaces and directories, versus facts checked, monthly
watch.source: facts list in the brand brain checked against Shopify, Google Merchant Center and marketplace listings

drives.metric: share of assistant answers that name the brand with correct facts

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 14 of 20 facts match everywhere. After: 20 of 20 after fixing the Amazon listing and the Merchant Center feed.

jobs.job: Make sure shopping assistants show the right price, stock and delivery
jobs.why: AI shopping features read product feeds. A stale feed shows the wrong price or 'in stock' on a sold-out item, which costs the sale and trust.

watch.metric: product fields (price, stock, shipping) that match the live store on a weekly spot check
watch.source: Google Merchant Center feed against Shopify

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 12% of products show a wrong price or stock status in the feed. After: feed synced daily, under 1%.

jobs.job: Know how many visits and sales AI assistants send
jobs.why: Without a count, the owner cannot tell if AI answers are worth any money or time. The count also shows which 1 to 3 assistants matter for our buyers.

watch.metric: visits and orders from AI assistants, by assistant, 30 day
watch.source: GA4 channel group for AI referrers, plus a 'how did you hear about us' question in Shopify checkout

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: AI visits hide inside 'referral'. After: 1,800 visits and 54 orders a month, 70% from ChatGPT.

jobs.job: Catch negative threads that assistants are quoting
jobs.why: Assistants often pull from Reddit and review sites. One unanswered complaint thread can shape every answer about the brand.

watch.metric: share of brand mentions in assistant answers that are negative, monthly, by assistant
watch.source: brand brain: monthly prompt-run log (a fixed set of buyer questions asked of each assistant; no platform reports this, so it is the closest proxy)

drives.metric: share of prompts where the brand is recommended

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Perplexity quotes a 2-year-old 'holes after a month' thread in 1 of 3 answers. After: a public reply and newer reviews drop it from answers in 2 months.

jobs.job: Check that a correction actually landed
jobs.why: Fixing the site is half the job. Assistants update on their own schedule, so each fix needs a recheck, or the wrong fact keeps costing sales.

watch.metric: corrections confirmed on recheck, and days from fix to confirmed
watch.source: brand brain corrections log with monthly rechecks

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5 fixes made, none rechecked. After: 4 of 5 confirmed within 30 days, 1 escalated to the source publisher.

jobs.job: Screen an AI visibility vendor pitch before signing
jobs.why: AI search vendors sell with new, untested numbers. Checking their claim against our own prompt runs and visits avoids paying for noise.

watch.metric: vendor claim versus our own prompt-run and AI visit numbers
watch.source: brand brain prompt-run log and GA4

drives.metric: AI visibility spend with no measured return

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a vendor promises '5x AI visibility'. After: our baseline shows we are already named in 60% of prompts, and the pitch is dropped.

jobs.job: Make sure Bing indexes our money pages
jobs.why: Some assistants search Bing to answer live questions. A store that is only checked in Google can be missing where those answers come from.

watch.metric: money pages indexed in Bing, monthly

drives.metric: share of assistant answers that cite our site

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 55% of money pages indexed in Bing. After: sitemap submitted and fixes done, 95%.

jobs.job: Send shoppers who follow made-up AI links to the right page
jobs.why: Assistants sometimes invent product URLs. Those clicks land on 'not found' and leave.

watch.metric: visits from AI assistants that land on a 'not found' page, 30 day

drives.metric: conversion rate of AI assistant visits

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 240 AI visits a month land on 'not found'. After: redirects to the closest real page, under 20.

jobs.job: Get recommended when buyers ask what to buy in our category
jobs.why: Being named is not enough. Buyers act on the brand the assistant recommends for their need, like 'best socks for standing all day'.

watch.metric: share of category buying prompts where the brand is recommended, monthly, by assistant
watch.source: brand brain: monthly prompt-run log (a fixed set of buyer questions asked of each assistant; no platform reports this, so it is the closest proxy)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: we are named in 50% of prompts but recommended in 15%. After: comparison pages and more reviews lift recommendations to 30% in 2 quarters.

jobs.job: See weekly how assistants describe named competitors
jobs.why: When an assistant starts calling a rival 'the best value' or repeats a new claim of theirs, our share of recommendations can drop before we notice.

watch.metric: our share of brand mentions versus named competitors, and new competitor claims, weekly
watch.source: brand brain: monthly prompt-run log (a fixed set of buyer questions asked of each assistant; no platform reports this, so it is the closest proxy)

drives.metric: share of prompts where the brand is recommended

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no watch on rivals. After: a weekly note shows a rival is now called 'most durable', and we answer with our test data.

jobs.job: Collect honest reviews on the sites assistants read
jobs.why: Assistants lean on review sites and marketplaces to judge quality. Few recent reviews there make the brand look weaker than it is.

watch.metric: review count and rating on the review sites assistants cite, 90 day
watch.source: reviews app, Google Business Profile and marketplace seller tools

drives.metric: share of prompts where the brand is recommended

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 40 reviews on the site assistants cite most. After: a post-purchase ask adds 300 in a quarter.

jobs.job: Make our top pages easy for an assistant to quote
jobs.why: Assistants lift short, direct answers. A page that buries the answer under brand story gets skipped for a competitor's clear one.

watch.metric: assistant citations to our 10 most visited pages, monthly
watch.source: brand brain: monthly prompt-run log (a fixed set of buyer questions asked of each assistant; no platform reports this, so it is the closest proxy)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 of our top 10 pages is ever cited. After: each opens with a direct answer and 5 are cited.

jobs.job: Build honest comparison pages against bigger rivals
jobs.why: Buyers ask assistants 'X or Y'. Without our own fair comparison, the answer is written from the rival's pages.

watch.metric: share of 'us versus rival' and 'alternatives to rival' prompts that name us, monthly
watch.source: brand brain: monthly prompt-run log (a fixed set of buyer questions asked of each assistant; no platform reports this, so it is the closest proxy)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: named in 1 of 8 comparison prompts. After: 3 comparison pages and we are named in 5 of 8.

jobs.job: Get onto the lists, reviews and threads assistants already cite
jobs.why: Assistants often cite a few 'best of' lists and forum threads for a category. Being absent from them means being absent from the answer.

watch.metric: cited third-party pages for our category that mention us, monthly
watch.source: brand brain: monthly prompt-run log (a fixed set of buyer questions asked of each assistant; no platform reports this, so it is the closest proxy)

drives.metric: share of prompts where the brand is recommended

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 of the 15 most cited pages mention us. After: outreach and samples get us onto 6.

jobs.job: Test one change with a control before calling an AI tactic a win
jobs.why: AI answers change on their own each month. Without a comparison group, the team will credit or blame the wrong work.

watch.metric: citation rate of changed pages versus similar unchanged pages, 8 weeks
watch.source: brand brain: monthly prompt-run log (a fixed set of buyer questions asked of each assistant; no platform reports this, so it is the closest proxy)

drives.metric: AI visibility spend that is proven to work

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 'we added FAQs and got cited' with no control. After: 10 test pages versus 10 control pages show a 2-point gain.
